sections.html:
A direct cash sale is the fastest route for a Spring Township house, but the township's property transfer inspection has to be scheduled either way. Spring Township is in Berks County, west of Reading, and it requires an exterior inspection of every single and multiple family dwelling before title changes hands. That inspection is the step that most often decides the calendar, so it comes first here.

The housing market is steady. There are 11,495 households, 75.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $286,900. Median rent is $1,416 and median household income is $94,837. About a quarter of homes are rented, so some sellers are small landlords who should check lease dates before setting a closing date.

This is a required exterior check under the township's Property Transfer Ordinance 341, in effect since August 1, 2007. The Code Enforcement Officer must inspect before title transfers. The seller, the buyer or either side's agent can file the application.

The application goes to the Code and Zoning Office no later than 30 business days before settlement. The fee is $150 per property, and it rises to $250 if the application arrives fewer than 15 business days before settlement. After a complete application, the officer inspects within 10 business days.

  • Utility and storm drainage easements and road rights-of-way must be clear of obstructions, including landscaping.
  • Fences, pools, spas, sheds and decks must be permitted and sit within setback and yard rules. Pool fencing needs a self-closing, latching gate.
  • Sanitary sewer connections must control inflow and infiltration, and sump pump discharge must be properly placed.
  • The number of dwelling units, bedrooms and smoke detectors is checked against township records.

When the application is filedInspection feeInspector's response
30 business days or more before settlement$150Within 10 business days

The inspection covers only exterior, observable conditions, and nobody has to be home as long as the inspector can reach the backyard. Add a note with a phone number to the application if you want to be there.

Seller and buyer both sign the report to confirm they read it and agree to correct what it lists, and the township then issues a Property Transfer Certificate once the deficiencies are done. That can happen before or after settlement.

You do not have to fix everything before closing. If the buyer is willing to take on the repairs, an addendum to the agreement of sale normally settles who is responsible and how the money works. Order the inspection soon after you decide to sell, because the report has to be disclosed to the buyer and an early look leaves time to permit anything that was built without approval.

Common findings are an unpermitted shed or deck, a fence in an easement, or a pool without the right barrier. Fixing a pool gate or moving a fence is usually quick, while an unpermitted deck may need a permit application first, so start those items early. Those are fixable, and a cash buyer who plans to renovate will often accept them as part of an as-is purchase.

sections.h2: Township rules that can surprise a seller
sections.html:
Spring Township reviews more than 700 permits a year and enforces its fence, shed and pool rules closely. Fences in a front yard are limited to 4 feet and must be open style, rear-yard fences can reach 6 feet, and sheds are not allowed in required front or side yards.

Residential grass and weeds may not exceed 8 inches. After a verified complaint the township sends a notice, cuts the property after 7 days if the owner does not, and bills the owner, and unpaid amounts become a lien on the real estate. Sidewalks must be cleared of snow and ice within 24 hours after it stops, with the same lien risk. Clear both before you list so the inspection comes back clean.

County and municipal tax payments can be made online through the Berks County Treasurer, and Wilson School District taxes are paid at Fulton Bank. Call the township tax collector's office for a payoff figure before closing. School real estate tax is paid separately from county and township tax.

Pennsylvania charges a 1 percent state realty transfer tax, collected with any local share by the Berks County Recorder of Deeds when the deed is recorded. Ask the Recorder for the combined local rate, and expect the buyer and seller to split it unless the sales agreement says otherwise.

The Wilson School District serves the township, with five elementary schools, two middle schools and Wilson High School. Spring Township borders Wyomissing, Sinking Spring and Adamstown, and U.S. 222, U.S. 422 and Route 724 cross it. A house near a main road or the bypass reads differently from one in a quiet subdivision, so say which you have in any listing or offer discussion. Terrain varies, with creeks to the north and hills toward the southwest, so lot grade and drainage can come up in an inspection.

sections.h2: A step-by-step plan for a Spring Township sale
sections.html:
1. Walk the exterior and list anything built without a permit, such as a shed, deck, fence or pool barrier.
  2. File the transfer inspection application with the Code and Zoning Office at least 30 business days before settlement to hold the fee at $150.
  3. Clear easements and rights-of-way of landscaping, and mow grass and weeds to under 8 inches.
  4. When the report arrives, read it with the buyer, sign it, and agree in an addendum who handles each item.
  5. Call the tax collector for a payoff figure, and ask the Recorder of Deeds for the local transfer tax rate.
  6. Wait for the Property Transfer Certificate, which the township issues once deficiencies are done, before or after settlement.

A cash buyer removes the mortgage appraisal step, though the township inspection still applies. If time is short and you file with fewer than 15 business days to go, expect the $250 fee. Keep the signed report, any permits you pull and the addendum together, because the title company and the buyer may both ask to see them. If tenants live in the house, give them notice that an inspector will be on the grounds, and check lease end dates before you agree to a settlement day.

faqs.q: Does Spring Township require an inspection to sell a house?
faqs.a: Yes. Ordinance 341 requires an exterior property transfer inspection by the Code Enforcement Officer before title changes. Apply at least 30 business days before settlement to pay the $150 fee.

faqs.q: What is the late fee for a Spring Township transfer inspection?
faqs.a: The fee is $250 instead of $150 when the application arrives fewer than 15 business days before settlement. The inspector still responds within 10 business days of a complete application.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix every item before closing?
faqs.a: No. A buyer can agree to make the corrections, and an addendum to the agreement of sale usually covers it. The Property Transfer Certificate is issued once the deficiencies are completed, before or after settlement.

faqs.q: Who can file the transfer inspection application?
faqs.a: The seller, the buyer or either side's agent. It goes to the Code and Zoning Office, and nobody has to be home as long as the inspector can reach the backyard.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Spring Township?
faqs.a: The Wilson School District serves the township, with five elementary schools, two middle schools and Wilson High School. School real estate tax is paid separately from county and township tax.
